subsystems.name: Photon source
subsystems.role: emits the faint laser pulses, or true entangled pairs, that carry the key.
parts: laser and attenuator, or spontaneous parametric down-conversion crystal

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: carries single photons without letting them be copied — optical fibre underground, or free space to a satellite.
parts: low-loss telecom fibre or telescope link
optical amplifiers avoided (they would break the protocol)

subsystems.name: Detectors
subsystems.role: catch individual photons and record their quantum state.
parts: superconducting nanowire or InGaAs avalanche photodiodes

subsystems.name: Classical channel
subsystems.role: public but authenticated link used to compare measurement bases, correct errors and distil the key.

subsystems.name: Key management
subsystems.role: turns raw correlated bits into keys and delivers them to the right users.
parts: key store and API for encrypting traffic

subsystems.name: Range extenders
subsystems.role: bridge distances beyond what a single fibre span can carry.
parts: quantum repeaters and memories (in the lab)

buildSteps.title: Generate the quantum states
buildSteps.detail: A laser is attenuated so that on average less than one photon per pulse travels, or a nonlinear crystal splits one photon into an entangled pair.

buildSteps.title: Transmit
buildSteps.detail: Photons go down dark fibre, or from a ground station to a satellite and back, with losses growing exponentially with distance.

buildSteps.title: Measure
buildSteps.detail: The receiver randomly picks a measurement basis for each photon and records the result.

buildSteps.title: Reconcile
buildSteps.detail: Sender and receiver publicly compare which bases were used, discard the rest, and correct the mismatches.

buildSteps.title: Detect eavesdropping
buildSteps.detail: Any interception disturbs the states and raises the error rate; past a threshold the key is thrown away.

buildSteps.title: Distil the key
buildSteps.detail: Privacy amplification shrinks the surviving bits into a short key that an eavesdropper has negligible information about.

buildSteps.title: Encrypt traffic
buildSteps.detail: The key drives a one-time pad or rekeys symmetric encryption between the two endpoints.

buildSteps.title: Scale out
buildSteps.detail: Metropolitan rings are linked by trusted nodes, and research aims to replace those nodes with quantum repeaters for a true mesh.

prerequisites.why: commercial QKD hardware depends on reliably detecting individual photons.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss fibre and satellite optical links
prerequisites.why: photon loss sets the maximum distance for a single span.
storing and releasing entangled photons is needed to synchronise repeater segments, and remains short-lived in the lab.
without them, long links rely on trusted nodes that are themselves hackable.
software-only quantum-resistant algorithms (NIST standards finalised in 2024) are the pragmatic alternative for most traffic.

pathway.milestone: metropolitan QKD links and national testbeds, plus satellite QKD demonstrated by China's Micius mission from 2016 and the roughly 2,000 km Beijing–Shanghai trunk line
pathway.unlocks: point-to-point keys between fixed sites, and confidence in the hardware.

pathway.milestone: intercity backbones and satellite constellations, and Europe's EuroQCI programme
pathway.unlocks: key distribution between cities and across regions, still using trusted nodes.
genuine long-distance entanglement without trusted nodes.
a communication layer whose security rests on physics rather than computational hardness — a claim only valid once side channels and endpoint trust are engineered away.
